title: The Roman Custom of Charity
english: For it is your custom from the beginning to do good to all brothers in various ways, and to send supplies to many churches throughout the whole city; in this way you refresh the poor who are in need, and in this way you provide for brothers who are in metal [wealth].

Through these you send the first supplies, a custom handed down from fathers which Romans preserve among Romans; which not only your blessed bishop Soter maintained, but also increased, providing the abundance sent out to the saints, and with blessed words encouraging the suffering brothers as a fatherly, loving parent does.

In this letter also he mentions the letter of Clement to the Corinthians, declaring from of old that it is the custom to perform the reading of it for the church. He says, therefore: We lead the present Lord's Day, the holy day, in which we read your letter; which we shall always have reading to be admonished, just as we had the former written to us through Clement.

title: The Apostolic Planting and Forged Epistles
english: Having been made a planting from Peter and Paul, you harvested both Romans and Corinthians. For both of them, having planted us even into our own Corinth, taught identically.
And having taught similarly even into Italy, they bore witness at the same time. And yet the same [person] says these things concerning his own letters, as if they had been forged.

For I wrote, having been deemed worthy to write the letters of brothers. And the apostles of the devil have filled these with weeds: some things they take away, and some things they add; to which the 'woe' lies. It is not therefore a wonder if some have cast forged things upon even the Lord's [letters], since they have cast [attacks] upon those not such.

title: Description of the Epistles
english: Having made himself known to all, in which he represented himself through universal letters to the churches. Of these, the one to the Lacedaemonians is catechetical regarding orthodoxy, and foundational for peace and unity.

The one to the Athenians is an awakening of faith and of the way of life according to the Gospel; which, having grown small, he reproves, saying that they must be little ones departing from the Word, from whom he testifies of their leader Puplius regarding the persecutions that happened then. And he remembers Kodratus standing as their bishop after the one who testified, Puplius; testifying how, through his zeal, they had been gathered together and had received a rekindling of faith.

And he shows upon this, how even Dionysius the Areopagite, having been turned to faith by the apostle Paul according to what was made manifest in the deeds [Acts 17:34], was first entrusted with the oversight of the residence in Athens.

title: Summary of Letters
english: He sent letters to the resident aliens in Crete, and receives Philip as their bishop, while the great courage of the church under him is being testified; he reminds them to guard against the perversion of the heretics.

And regarding the church residing in Amastris, he sent letters to them by way of Pontus, and he remembers having urged Bakchylides and Elpis to write to him; he sets forth explanations of divine writings; he marks out Palman as their bishop; and he advises the same people much concerning marriage and chastity. He also commands that those who are turning back from whatever fall, whether from fault or from heretical error, should be received.

By these [means] another letter was sent toward the Knossians, in which he exhorts Pinutos, the bishop of the resident aliens, not to always lay the heavy burden of chastity upon the brothers, but to observe the weakness of the many.

And another letter of Dionysius is brought alongside these, having been sent to a most faithful sister, Chrysophoros. In which, by writing the appropriate things, she also shared in the logical food that was fitting for her.
